title: First load lists tiers by number, archived in archive order, then the rest
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin whose role has 'Reports — Page Access', 'Settings — Parts', 'See Financial Data', 'Customers — View', 'Customers — Create & Edit', 'Work Orders — Order Parts' and 'Work Order Lines — Create & Edit'.
  • Have a new category for this test, category A, priced by a new matrix for this test, matrix A, with one cost range ($0.00 and up) whose Default rule is Markup % 35.
  • Have a new tier for this test, tier A, with a name no other tier uses, whose column in matrix A is % Off 10.
  • Have a new tier for this test, tier B, with a name no other tier uses, whose column in matrix A is % Off 20, made after tier A.
  • Have a new tier for this test, tier C, with a name no other tier uses, whose column in matrix A is % Off 30.
  • Have a new tier for this test, tier D, with a name no other tier uses, whose column in matrix A is % Off 40.
  • Have new customers for this test, customers A, B, C and D, each put on the tier with its letter for work orders, and customer E left on Default.
  • Have a new work order for this test, invoiced today, for each of customers A to E, each with one part in category A, cost $100.00; customer E's work order also has a fixed-price part, a part with a typed price and a fixed line total.
  • Make sure tier D was archived first and tier C second, after their customers were moved to Default and their work orders invoiced.
  • Use a desktop browser window at least 1440 pixels wide, at 100% zoom, so every column of the page shows.
custom_steps:
1. Open Reports › Sales by Tier.
  2. Pick customers A to E in the Customer filter.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Sales by Tier opens.

Step 2:

  • Rows read, in order: Default, tier A, tier B, tier D (archived), tier C (archived), Fixed price, Fixed line total, Manual.
